original_source_field:
Commissioner v. Kowalski, 434 U.S. 77 (1977) — https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/434/77/
Internal Revenue Code of 1954, 26 U.S.C. § 61(a) and § 119
original_excerpt: In Commissioner v. Kowalski, 434 U.S. 77, 84, 90–94 (1977), the Supreme Court ruled that cash meal allowances paid to state troopers constitute gross income under § 61(a) and are not subject to exclusion under § 119 of the Internal Revenue Code. The Court determined that § 119 covers only meals furnished in kind by the employer, not cash allowances or cash reimbursements, and that the enactment of § 119 ended any nonstatutory convenience-of-the-employer doctrine for cash payments.
fidelity: Income and §119 in-kind/cash distinction supported. 'Ended any nonstatutory ... doctrine for cash payments' should be bounded to the prior convenience rationale and allowances at issue.
scope_note: Preserve reserved other grounds and sporadic meal reimbursement; avoid universal cash-benefit rule.
previous_record_verification: No previous in-scope closure relied on.
